background, since its whole process group is ended with it.

        A background command that never ends on its own, as a dev server
        started with `npm run dev`, `vite`, or `node server.js`, or a watcher,
        never keeps a task running once its work is done. Once a result has
        come, every message sent has been taken in, and no subagent is still
        going, a background command still running holds the run open only
        while it is busy: one that has printed nothing for 60 seconds since
        that result, as a server does once it has started and waits for
        requests, is taken as idle. Once every background task left is an
        idle command, the run asks the harness to stop each of them, as a
        single background task is stopped above, and once their ends are
        notified, the result that came is the run's last, and the task
        finishes in its state, done where it was. A command that keeps
        printing, as a long build or test run does, keeps the run open until
        it ends or goes quiet. While the run waits on background commands
        and nothing else, the task's status still reads "Running", and its
        tooltip says it is waiting on background commands, naming how many,
        which the subagents panel lists with their Stop buttons.

        A harness's process that hasn't exited 10 seconds after the run's
        last result, with its input closed, as when a server it started still
        holds its output open, is ended with its whole process group, and
        the task finishes in the state of that last result, never left
        running. Whatever the run started is ended with it: no server a task
        started is left running once the task is shown as finished, so its
        port is free again.

use /lib
from ../project-data import ProjectDataScope
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from ../prompt-mode/ask-conversation import AskConversationScope
from ../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts import ModeSystemPromptsScope
from ../prompt-mode/sending import PromptSendingScope
from ../settings-window import SettingsWindowScope
from ../user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope
from ./baked-prompts import BakedSystemPromptsScope
from ./catalog import HarnessCatalogScope
from ./one-off-run import OneOffAgentRunScope
from /scope/container-environment import ContainerEnvironmentScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from /ui/components/task-table import TaskTableScope

export scope HarnessIntegrationScope:
    concept: {HarnessIntegrationConcept}

concept HarnessIntegrationConcept:
    pitch:
        Uses the one-off version of a coding harness for the selected
        ${ProjectDirectoryScope}: `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `opencode run`,
        whichever the user chose. Each run carries on a conversation, so the
        harness keeps its context between requests.

    shape: {HarnessIntegrationShape}

shape HarnessIntegrationShape:
    description:
        Should always run in auto mode.

        The project's system prompt, its system template filled in, as the
        @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says, is appended to the harness's own
        system prompt, for example with `--append-system-prompt`, the same for
        every prompt of a conversation whatever its mode. The compiled
        systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor, its mode's instructions,
        heads the prompt's own message instead.

        The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the
        harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its
        prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be
        fed more while it works, as its feeding says.

        Its directory, which a system prompt's HARNESS_DIRECTORY stands for,
        is that of the harness in use: .claude, .codex, or .opencode.

        Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps and spec follow-up, and
        questions always run the harness in a container the application owns,
        as the @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, which holds only what their
        mode may use. Every other run, Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code
        step, always, with their protected locations, Freeform, and the
        application's own, runs the harness on the host, in the project directory. Either
        way the harness is run, prompted, and read just as this says.

    harnesses:
        The harness in use is the one picked in the @{SettingsWindowScope}:
        Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked.
        It is remembered for the user, as the @{UserPreferencesScope} says, not
        for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks,
        the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the
        notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything
        else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked
        finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only
        carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another
        harness starts a new one.

        Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of
        JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage,
        and result, whichever harness wrote it:

        - Claude Code is `claude -p`, in auto mode, the system prompt given
            with `--append-system-prompt`, a conversation carried on with
            `--resume`, and a copy of one with `--fork-session`.
        - Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt
            read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with
            `resume`.
        - OpenCode is `opencode run`, with `--format json`, a conversation
            carried on with `--session`.

        Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given
        ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of
        a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a
        new conversation with them instead. The notes, commit messages, and
        prompt titles are written with a small model where the harness can be
        told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.

        No run the application starts is given the connectors of the user's
        claude.ai account, such as Gmail, Google Calendar, or Google Drive,
        on the host or in a container, whatever the account has connected or
        left unauthorized: Claude Code is run with them turned off, with
        `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS` set to `false` in its environment. So
        the harness is never told that a connector needs authorizing or is
        still connecting, never searches for or calls one, and never passes
        such a notice on in what it replies, and nothing of the kind is ever
        shown in a task's output, a question's answer, or anywhere else. MCP
        servers the project itself configures for a run on the host are left
        as they are; a run in a container has none, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says.

        When the harness picked isn't installed, a run on the host fails
        saying that it can't be run, as any run that can't be started does. A
        run in a container uses the harness in its image instead, and fails,
        where Podman isn't installed or can't run, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says.

    protectedLocations:
        Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container
        has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the
        @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is
        given no rule against reading or editing anything.

        Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude
        Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its
        mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a
        Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever
        changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a
        passive notice, never an error, as the @{TaskTableScope} says. A Code
        task is also told it may not read the spec location, alongside that,
        so it reads the compiled reference instead, as the
        @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says. A question from the Ask tab always
        runs in a container, so it is never given this rule, nor any other
        telling it to keep off the spec location. This rule is only a nudge, and
        doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the
        files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that
        takes no such rules is told nothing of either.

    feeding:
        A task's run is given its prompt as a stream of messages: Claude Code
        with `--input-format stream-json`, each message written as a line of
        JSON on the harness's standard input, which stays open for as long as
        the run lasts. The run's first message is the task's compiled prompt,
        as ever, and each message sent to the task after it, from the
        @{ChatInputScope}, is written as another.

        A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather
        than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that
        call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in,
        with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is
        answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under
        way is answered within that turn, sharing its result.

        A run can also start work in the background that goes on after its
        turn ends: Claude Code's subagents, shell commands run in the
        background, such as a long build, and any other kind of background
        task it adds later. Every such task holds the run open, whatever its
        kind. The run keeps each background task that has started and not yet
        ended, by its id: one starts when the harness says a task has started,
        and ends when the harness notifies that task's end, whatever it ended
        as. A notification doesn't say what kind of task it is, so it is
        matched by id against those seen starting. The harness wakes the run
        when a background task ends, so it can act on what came of it.

        Each background task is known by its kind, from what started it: a
        subagent, started by an Agent or Task tool call, or a command, a shell
        command run in the background. Its start is when the harness said it
        had started, so how long it has been running can be told. A single
        background task can be stopped while the run goes on, without ending
        the run or any other task: the harness is asked, on the run's input,
        to stop that task by its id, Claude Code with its stream-json control
        request for stopping a task. The task then ends when the harness
        notifies its end, as ever, as stopped, and the harness carries on
        with what came of it. Stopping one is never done by stopping the
        harness's process, and a run whose input is already closed, or whose
        harness can't be fed, can't stop one on its own.

        A result no longer ends the task on its own. The run's last result is
        the first to come once every message sent has been taken in and no
        background task is still going. A result that comes before then, while
        a message sent hasn't been taken in or a background task is still
        going, is only an answer: the task keeps running, its input stays
        open, and more can still be sent to it. At the last result the run's
        input is closed, but the task is only shown as finished once the
        harness's process has exited as well, and it then finishes in the
        state of that last result; until the process exits, the task keeps
        running. A process that exits without a last result finishes the task
        as a run with no result does, failed. A run that is stopped closes its
        input and ends straight away, whatever is still going in the
        background, since its whole process group is ended with it.

        Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt
        and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either
        takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.

        Questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes,
        commit messages, and prompt titles each take a single prompt, as ever.

    images:
        Images attached to a prompt, as the @{ChatInputScope} says, are given
        to the harness as it takes them: to Claude Code as image content blocks,
        base64-encoded with their media type, in the same stream-json user
        message as the prompt's text, after it; to Codex with an `--image`
        argument per image; and to OpenCode with a `--file` argument per image.
        A message fed to a running Claude Code task carries its images the same
        way, and a Claude Code run that isn't fed more but has images is given
        its prompt as a stream-json message too, so the images can go with it.
        Codex's options end with `--` before the prompt when it is given
        images. Questions take images as tasks do.

    context:
        The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh
        each time. Each lane of the @{PromptSendingScope} carries on a
        conversation of its own, so nothing a task of one lane read reaches a
        task of the other: the spec lane's, carried on by Spec tasks and a
        Chain prompt's spec steps, and the code lane's, carried on by Code
        tasks, a Chain prompt's code step, and Freeform tasks. Each task sent
        carries on its own lane's, and since a lane runs one task at a time,
        two tasks never carry on the same conversation at once. A Chain
        prompt's steps hand on to each other as text, the prompt and what the
        step before replied, as the @{ModeSystemPromptsScope} says, so the
        handoff crosses lanes whatever each lane's conversation holds. When
        the project is opened, each lane carries on the latest conversation
        among its own tasks in the history, a Chain task by the lane of the
        step it was.

        The spec lane and the questions always run in a container, and the
        code lane always on the host, so each conversation is only ever
        carried on where it began. A run in a container keeps its
        conversation's sessions in the project, in its own folder of
        `.suspense/sessions/`, as the @{ContainerEnvironmentScope} says, so
        it carries on across runs, restarts of the application, and moves of
        the project; a run on the host keeps them where the harness keeps
        them on the host.

        Questions from the Ask tab share a separate
        conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on
        the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question
        asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation,
        so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A
        conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open
        project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is
        in the background. A spec lane or questions conversation from before
        its sessions were kept in the project, whose session the project's
        sessions folder doesn't hold, is still tried, and when the harness
        has no such session, the request is sent again at once as a new
        conversation, as below.

        A request whose conversation can't be carried on, because the
        harness says it has no such session, as Claude Code's "No
        conversation found", or because it was begun elsewhere, is never
        failed for it, and never retried on the same conversation: it is
        sent again at once as a new conversation, the same prompt, with no
        context, and the conversation it couldn't carry on is not tried
        again by any later request, the project's history included. A
        question sent again so is recorded and shown as starting a new
        conversation, as the @{AskConversationScope} marks one. Each run applies
        its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation
        begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts
        fresh.

        A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New

content.text:
The likeliest cause is that the agent started the dev server as a background command. The spec says every background command keeps a task running until it ends, and a server never ends, so the task stays "Running" forever. I added rules so a server can't hold a task open once the work is done. I also covered a run-target case with the same symptom, in case that's where you saw it. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 81 files.

## What changed in the spec

**Tasks** (`.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/index.md#feeding`)
- **Idle commands:** after the agent has given its result, all messages are taken in and no subagent is running, a background command that has printed nothing for 60 seconds counts as idle. That's what a server does once it has started.
- **Stopping them:** when only idle commands are left, Suspense asks the harness to stop each one by id. The result that already came becomes the last, and the task finishes as Done.
- **Busy commands still count:** a background build or test run that keeps printing still holds the task open until it ends or goes quiet.
- **While waiting:** the status still reads "Running", and its tooltip says how many background commands it's waiting on. They're listed with Stop buttons in the subagents panel.
- **Process timeout:** if the harness's process hasn't exited 10 seconds after the last result, for example because a server still holds its output open, it is ended with its whole process group. The task then finishes. No server a task started survives the task finishing, so its port is free.

**Run targets** (`.claude/reference/scope/run-targets/index.md#stopping`)
- A target is over when its command exits, not when its output closes. A leftover child holding the output open can't keep it at "Running". Whatever is left is stopped.
- A target whose command *is* the server keeps running until you stop it.

**My choices:** 60 seconds of silence and the 10-second exit timeout are my own numbers, so adjust them if they feel wrong.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791386842-NodeServerStuckRunning.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `HarnessIntegrationScope`: `#feeding`, for spotting idle commands, stopping them by id, the 10-second exit timeout and ending the process group.
- `SubagentsPanel`: `#description` and `#stopping`, where the waited-on commands are listed.
- `RunTargetsScope`: `#stopping`, for detecting the end by process exit.
